title: Handshaking lemma
conditions: Finite undirected graph; each loop, if present, contributes $2$ to degree.
meaning: The sum of all vertex degrees counts every edge twice.
example: A path on $4$ vertices has degrees $1,2,2,1$, so their sum is $6=2\cdot3$.
source: West, Introduction to Graph Theory (2nd ed.); standard result.

title: Average degree
conditions: Finite nonempty undirected graph.
meaning: Relates the average local degree to the total number of edges.
source: West, Introduction to Graph Theory (2nd ed.); standard result.

title: Edges of a complete graph
conditions: Simple complete graph with $n\ge1$ vertices.
meaning: Each unordered pair of distinct vertices contributes exactly one edge.
source: West, Introduction to Graph Theory (2nd ed.); standard result.

title: Edge count of a tree
conditions: Finite tree (connected and acyclic).
meaning: Every tree has exactly one fewer edge than vertices.
example: A tree with $10$ vertices has $9$ edges.
source: West, Introduction to Graph Theory (2nd ed.); standard result.

title: Euler formula for planar graphs
conditions: Connected graph with a fixed planar embedding; count the outer face.
meaning: Connects vertices, edges, and faces of a connected plane graph.
example: A square with one diagonal has $4$ vertices, $5$ edges and $3$ faces: $4-5+3=2$.
source: West, Introduction to Graph Theory (2nd ed.); standard result.

title: Adjacency matrix
conditions: Finite simple graph with an indexed vertex set.
meaning: Encodes edges in a matrix. For an undirected graph, $A=A^\mathsf T$.
source: Godsil & Royle, Algebraic Graph Theory; standard result.

title: Counting walks by matrix powers
conditions: Finite graph with adjacency matrix $A$; $k$ is a nonnegative integer.
meaning: Matrix multiplication counts successive choices of adjacent vertices.
source: Godsil & Royle, Algebraic Graph Theory; standard result.

title: Trace counts closed walks
conditions: Finite undirected graph; $A$ is its adjacency matrix and $\lambda_i$ its eigenvalues with multiplicity; integer $k\ge1$.
meaning: The trace also equals the number of closed walks of length $k$.
example: For $C_3$, $\operatorname{tr}(A^3)=6$: three starting vertices and two orientations.
source: Godsil & Royle, Algebraic Graph Theory; standard result.

title: Triangle count from adjacency spectrum
conditions: Finite simple undirected graph.
meaning: Each triangle gives six length-$3$ closed walks (three starting vertices and two directions).
source: Godsil & Royle, Algebraic Graph Theory; standard result.

title: Graph Laplacian
conditions: Finite undirected graph; $D=\operatorname{diag}(\deg(v_1),\ldots,\deg(v_n))$.
meaning: Subtracting the adjacency matrix from the degree matrix produces the combinatorial Laplacian.
source: Chung, Spectral Graph Theory; standard result.

title: Laplacian quadratic form
conditions: Finite simple undirected graph and real vector $x\in\mathbb R^{|V|}$.
meaning: Shows the graph Laplacian is positive semidefinite and measures variation across edges.
source: Chung, Spectral Graph Theory; standard result.

title: Zero eigenvalues and components
conditions: Finite undirected graph; $c(G)$ denotes its number of connected components.
meaning: The dimension of the Laplacian nullspace equals the number of components.
example: For the disjoint union $K_2\sqcup K_1$, the Laplacian eigenvalue $0$ has multiplicity $2$.
source: Chung, Spectral Graph Theory; standard result.

title: Algebraic connectivity
conditions: Undirected graph with $n\ge2$ and Laplacian eigenvalues $0=\lambda_1\le\lambda_2\le\cdots\le\lambda_n$.
meaning: The second-smallest Laplacian eigenvalue detects graph connectivity.
source: Chung, Spectral Graph Theory; standard result.

title: Matrix–tree theorem
conditions: Finite undirected graph; $L^{(v)}$ is obtained by deleting row and column $v$ from the Laplacian.
meaning: Any principal cofactor of the Laplacian counts spanning trees.
source: Godsil & Royle, Algebraic Graph Theory; standard result.

title: Cayley formula
conditions: Complete labeled graph $K_n$ with $n\ge2$.
meaning: Counts all labeled trees on a fixed set of $n$ vertices.
example: There are $4^{4-2}=16$ labeled trees on four vertices.
source: West, Introduction to Graph Theory (2nd ed.); standard result.

title: Eigenvalue of a regular graph
conditions: Undirected $d$-regular graph with adjacency matrix $A$.
meaning: The all-ones vector is an adjacency eigenvector with eigenvalue $d$.
source: Godsil & Royle, Algebraic Graph Theory; standard result.

title: Bipartite spectral symmetry
conditions: Finite undirected bipartite graph; eigenvalues counted with multiplicity.
meaning: The adjacency spectrum of a bipartite graph is symmetric about zero.
source: Godsil & Royle, Algebraic Graph Theory; standard result.

title: Chromatic polynomial of a tree
conditions: Tree with $n\ge1$ vertices; $k$ is a positive integer for counting proper colorings.
meaning: Choose any color for the root and then any color except its parent’s for each other vertex.
source: West, Introduction to Graph Theory (2nd ed.); standard result.

title: Laplacian trace and degrees
conditions: Finite simple undirected graph and combinatorial Laplacian $L$.
meaning: The sum of the Laplacian eigenvalues equals twice the number of edges.
source: Chung, Spectral Graph Theory; standard result.

title: Adjacency eigenvalue square sum
conditions: Finite simple undirected graph.
meaning: The sum of squared adjacency eigenvalues counts oriented edge traversals.
source: Godsil & Royle, Algebraic Graph Theory; standard result.

title: Complement adjacency matrix
conditions: Finite simple graph on $n$ vertices; $J$ is the $n\times n$ all-ones matrix.
meaning: Off-diagonal adjacency in the complement is exactly non-adjacency in the original graph.
example: The complement of $K_n$ has adjacency matrix $0=J-I-(J-I)$.
source: Godsil & Royle, Algebraic Graph Theory; standard result.

title: Normalized Laplacian
conditions: Finite undirected graph with no isolated vertices (so $D^{-1/2}$ is defined).
meaning: Degree normalization produces a Laplacian whose eigenvalues are in $[0,2]$.
source: Chung, Spectral Graph Theory; standard result.

title: Eigenvalue and eigenvector
conditions: Square matrix $A$; scalars and vectors over a field containing $\lambda$.
meaning: An eigenvector changes only by a scalar factor under the linear map.
source: Strang, Introduction to Linear Algebra; standard result.

title: Characteristic polynomial
conditions: Square $n\times n$ matrix $A$.
meaning: Its roots, counted with algebraic multiplicity, are precisely the eigenvalues of $A$.
source: Strang, Introduction to Linear Algebra; standard result.

title: Trace as the sum of eigenvalues
conditions: Square matrix over $\mathbb C$ (or use eigenvalues in an algebraic closure), with algebraic multiplicities.
meaning: The diagonal sum equals the sum of all eigenvalues even when $A$ is not diagonalizable.
source: Strang, Introduction to Linear Algebra; standard result.

title: Determinant as the product of eigenvalues
conditions: Square matrix, with eigenvalues in an algebraic closure and counted with algebraic multiplicity.
meaning: The determinant vanishes exactly when zero is an eigenvalue.
source: Strang, Introduction to Linear Algebra; standard result.

title: Rank–nullity theorem
conditions: Matrix $A$ with $n$ columns, representing a linear map with $n$-dimensional domain.
meaning: The dimensions of the image and kernel add to the domain dimension.
source: Strang, Introduction to Linear Algebra; standard result.

title: Spectral theorem for real symmetric matrices
conditions: Real symmetric $n\times n$ matrix; $Q$ orthogonal and $\Lambda$ real diagonal.
meaning: Every real symmetric matrix has an orthonormal eigenbasis.
source: Strang, Introduction to Linear Algebra; standard result.

title: Cayley–Hamilton theorem
conditions: Square matrix $A$ with characteristic polynomial $p_A$.
meaning: A matrix satisfies its own characteristic polynomial.
source: Horn & Johnson, Matrix Analysis; standard result.

title: Cyclic property of trace
conditions: Matrices $A\in\mathbb F^{m\times n}$ and $B\in\mathbb F^{n\times m}$.
meaning: The trace does not change when a product of two compatible matrices is cyclically reordered.
example: For $A=(1\ \ 2)$ and $B=(3\ \ 4)^\mathsf T$, both traces equal $11$.
source: Horn & Johnson, Matrix Analysis; standard result.

title: Multiplicativity of determinant
conditions: Square matrices $A,B$ of equal size over a commutative field.
meaning: The determinant of a composition is the product of determinants.
source: Strang, Introduction to Linear Algebra; standard result.

title: Invertibility criterion
conditions: Square matrix $A$ over a field.
meaning: An invertible matrix has full rank and no zero eigenvalue.
example: The matrix $\begin{pmatrix}1&2\\2&4\end{pmatrix}$ is singular because its determinant is $0$.
source: Strang, Introduction to Linear Algebra; standard result.

title: Orthogonal projection onto a column space
conditions: Real matrix $A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}$ with linearly independent columns.
meaning: Projects vectors in $\mathbb R^m$ orthogonally onto the column space of $A$.
source: Strang, Introduction to Linear Algebra; standard result.

title: Least-squares solution (full column rank)
conditions: Real matrix $A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}$ with full column rank; vector $b\in\mathbb R^m$.
meaning: Minimizes $\|Ax-b\|_2^2$ and solves the normal equations.
source: Strang, Introduction to Linear Algebra; standard result.

title: Singular value decomposition
conditions: Real $m\times n$ matrix; $U,V$ orthogonal and $\Sigma$ rectangular diagonal with nonnegative singular values.
meaning: Decomposes any real matrix into orthogonal changes of basis and axis scaling.
source: Strang, Introduction to Linear Algebra; standard result.

title: Frobenius norm
conditions: Real matrix $A$ (use conjugate transpose and $|a_{ij}|^2$ for complex matrices).
meaning: The squared Frobenius norm is the sum of the squared matrix entries.
source: Strang, Introduction to Linear Algebra; standard result.

title: Power traces and eigenvalues
conditions: Square matrix $A$ and integer $k\ge1$; eigenvalues counted algebraically.
meaning: The trace of any positive integer power equals the corresponding spectral power sum.
source: Horn & Johnson, Matrix Analysis; standard result.

title: Similarity preserves characteristic polynomial
conditions: Square $A$ and invertible matrix $P$ of the same size.
meaning: A change of basis does not change eigenvalues or the characteristic polynomial.
example: The diagonal matrix $\operatorname{diag}(1,2)$ is similar to $\operatorname{diag}(2,1)$.
source: Strang, Introduction to Linear Algebra; standard result.

title: Geometric vs. algebraic multiplicity
conditions: $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue of a square matrix $A$; $m_{\mathrm{alg}}$ is its multiplicity as a root of $p_A$.
meaning: An eigenspace cannot have dimension greater than its eigenvalue’s characteristic-polynomial multiplicity.
example: For $A=\begin{pmatrix}2&1\\0&2\end{pmatrix}$, algebraic multiplicity is $2$ but eigenspace dimension is $1$.
source: Horn & Johnson, Matrix Analysis; standard result.

title: Positive semidefinite criterion
conditions: Real symmetric matrix $A$; $A\succeq0$ means $x^\mathsf TAx\ge0$ for all real $x$.
meaning: A real symmetric matrix is positive semidefinite exactly when all eigenvalues are nonnegative.
source: Horn & Johnson, Matrix Analysis; standard result.

title: Matrix determinant lemma
conditions: Invertible real $n\times n$ matrix $A$ and vectors $u,v\in\mathbb R^n$.
meaning: Computes the determinant after a rank-one update.
example: For $A=I_2$ and $u=v=(1,0)^\mathsf T$, the determinant is $2$.
source: Horn & Johnson, Matrix Analysis; standard result.

title: Orthogonality of distinct eigenvectors
conditions: Real symmetric matrix $A$, with eigenvectors corresponding to distinct eigenvalues $\lambda,\mu$.
meaning: Eigenvectors of a real symmetric matrix from different eigenspaces are orthogonal.
example: For $A=\operatorname{diag}(2,3)$, $(1,0)^\mathsf T$ and $(0,1)^\mathsf T$ are orthogonal.
source: Strang, Introduction to Linear Algebra; standard result.

title: Trace in the characteristic polynomial
conditions: Square $n\times n$ matrix $A$ with monic characteristic polynomial $p_A(t)=\det(tI-A)$.
meaning: The coefficient of the next-to-highest term is the negative trace.
source: Horn & Johnson, Matrix Analysis; standard result.

title: Eigenvalues of an inverse
conditions: Invertible square matrix $A$ and a nonzero eigenvector $v$.
meaning: Taking the inverse reciprocates nonzero eigenvalues and preserves eigenvectors.
source: Strang, Introduction to Linear Algebra; standard result.
